subject: Proposal: hosted API latency thresholds & measurement granularity for FinPay pilot
messages:
From: ops@finpay.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-15T10:11:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API SLOs for pilot — need concrete numbers

Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're close to finalizing procurement for a two-week pilot and Procurement asked us to lock down specific latency commitments for the hosted API (p50 / p95) and how Redwood plans to measure them. A couple of things they care about:

- Measurement window and aggregation rules (rolling vs fixed buckets)
- Treatment of cold starts, retries, and streaming responses
- Whether model fallback or quantized variants count as service failures

Can you send a short proposal with concrete targets and measurement methodology we can attach to the pilot statement of work? We're targeting low-latency user flows for payments validation (tight 200ms budget end-to-end ideally), so being explicit here will help us align internally.

Attaching our internal SLA template for reference (not attached here in the thread).

Best,
Sam R.
Sam Rivera
Head of Ops — FinPay
ops@finpay.com
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: ops@finpay.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-15T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs for pilot — need concrete numbers

Sam —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've sketched a succinct proposal below and attached a short draft PDF and a CSV sample of how we'd compute windows from our telemetry. High level recommendations for the pilot (two-week, hosted, US region):

- Proposed Targets: p50 = 40 ms, p95 = 240 ms (measured at Redwood egress — client-facing response time).
- Measurement: rolling 30-minute window with 1-second aggregation granularity. Final p50/p95 computed from the population of successful, non-redirected responses in the window.
- Cold-start carveout: requests originating within the first 10 minutes of a routing scale event are excluded from the window; we also exclude requests that have a KV-cache miss on models where cold cache materially impacts latency (we emit a cold_start boolean).
- Streaming: streaming tokens are measured at initial response latency for p50/p95; token-stream duration is tracked separately for observability, not in the primary SLO.
- Retries: client-triggered retries count as separate attempts; we deduplicate by request-id where provided and only count the final successful attempt. Retries due to network between client and Redwood (5xx at our egress) are counted as failures.
- Model fallback: if we automatically fall back to a lower-capacity model variant for capacity or regional reasons but still return a 200 response, that response is considered in-bounds (not a failure), but we will surface model_variant in the telemetry and offer a negotiated carveout if fallback becomes frequent (>1% of requests over a 24h window).

Operational commitments / pilot mechanics:

- Two-week pilot with weekly checkpoints (Mon standups).
- SLA credit: for a region-level p95 breach sustained across three consecutive 30-minute windows, we propose a pro-rated credit for the pilot scope only.
- Rollback & mitigation: automated fallback to a lower-tier serving pool after sustained queueing; routing to alternate region as emergency fallback (will be opt-in).

I attached: SLO_proposal_finpay_v1.pdf (details + sample calculation) and sample_windowed_metrics.csv. If this looks reasonable, I'll incorporate any edits from Laura and send a revised draft with DocuSign for signatures.

Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk Procurement and DevOps through metrics?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-15T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API SLOs for pilot — need concrete numbers

Rishi — forwarding quick in-line suggestions from Sales perspective. I'm fine with the structure, but recommend tightening and clarifying a couple of points before we send to FinPay: 

1) Targets: tighten p50 to 30–40ms range but we shouldn't promise <30ms at scale unless it's verified in the FinPay flow; suggest we land on p50 = 40 ms to be conservative.
2) Carveouts: for large onboarding spikes (first-hour traffic surges driven by batch imports) extend the cold-start carveout to 60 minutes and mark that as a one-time onboarding carveout (we'll track usage).
3) Measurement: call out that measurement is computed per-route (per API endpoint) and aggregated to account-level for contractual queries; i.e., an endpoint with streaming behavior should have its own SLO line item.
4) Credits: make the pilot credit limited to setup fees and pro-rated usage (to keep negotiation simple).

I'll be explicit in the draft PDF edits; once updated, send to Sam with a short bullet list and DocuSign link.

Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: ops@finpay.com, cto@finpay.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-16T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Final: Hosted API SLO proposal & next steps (FinPay pilot)

Sam / Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and thanks Laura for the edits. Attached is FinPay_SLO_Draft_v2.pdf which reflects the updated items below (summary):

- Targets: p50 = 40 ms (egress), p95 = 240 ms (egress).
- Windows: rolling 30-minute windows, 1-second aggregation. p50/p95 computed over successful responses; per-route SLOs roll up to account-level.
- Carveouts: 10-minute automatic cold-start carveout on routing scale events; one-time onboarding carveout up to 60 minutes for heavy batch imports (must be scheduled and logged).
- Treatment of fallback: successful fallback responses count toward SLO; frequent fallback (>1% over 24h) will trigger a remediation plan and optional carveout discussion.
- Streaming: initial token latency counted for SLO; full-stream duration tracked for ops-only metrics.

Pilot mechanics / acceptance:

1) Two-week pilot starting once both sides sign the attached DocuSign (link below).
2) Weekly check-ins (30m) with DevOps and our CS engineer (Marissa).
3) If p95 is breached for three consecutive 30-minute windows region-wide, we'll issue a pro-rated credit scoped to pilot fees and usage for that period.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/FinPay-SLO-FP-4932
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/6543210/deal/FP-4932

Please confirm acceptance of the summary above and I'll route the DocuSign. If you prefer, we can hop on a 30-minute call at 11:00 PT today.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
